title: Places and Clear Instructions
subtitle: A practical English revision pack for describing places and giving simple directions.

days.title: Day 1 — Describe where things are
days.intro: Use simple place words to say where people and things are.

activities.title: A place phrase adds useful detail
activities.instructions: Read each sentence aloud. Point to an object near you if you can.
activities.content:
Use in for a space: “The keys are in the bag.”
Use on for a surface: “The phone is on the table.”
Use under for a lower position: “The shoes are under the chair.”
Use next to for a close position: “The bank is next to the café.”
Use between for a middle position: “The shop is between the pharmacy and the station.”
Use opposite for a place across from another place: “The bus stop is opposite the park.”

activities.title: Place prepositions: in, on, under, next to, between
activities.instructions: Choose the best place word. Use the sentence picture in your mind.
activities.content:
A useful question is: “Where is it?” A useful answer starts with: “It is…”
“Where is the notebook?” “It is on the desk.”
“Where is the station?” “It is next to the museum.”

questions.prompt: Choose the best answer: “The cup is ___ the table.”
Choose the best answer: “The cat is ___ the chair.”

activities.title: Useful words for places
activities.instructions: Read the words. You will meet them again in the reading and dialogue.
activities.content:
entrance — where you go in
exit — where you go out
corner — where two streets meet
stairs — steps between floors
lift — a small room that moves between floors
station — a place for trains or buses
pharmacy — a shop for medicine
receipt — a paper that shows what you bought

activities.title: Reading: finding a place in a building
activities.instructions: Read once. Then find the place words in the text.
activities.content: Ava is in a large building for the first time. The entrance is opposite the bus stop. Inside, the lift is next to the stairs. Ava needs the office on the second floor. The office is between a small café and a pharmacy. Her appointment note is in her bag, and her phone is on the desk in the waiting area.

options: On a desk in the waiting area

activities.title: Dialogue: asking where something is
activities.instructions: Read both roles. Then change the place or object in [brackets].

dialogue.speaker: Ava
dialogue.text: Excuse me. Where is the [lift], please?

dialogue.speaker: Guide
dialogue.text: It is next to the stairs.

dialogue.speaker: Ava
dialogue.text: Is it near the [entrance]?

dialogue.speaker: Guide
dialogue.text: Yes. It is opposite the café.

dialogue.speaker: Ava
dialogue.text: Thank you for your help.

days.title: Day 2 — Give clear instructions
days.intro: Use the imperative to tell someone what to do in a friendly, clear way.

activities.title: The imperative: start with the verb
activities.instructions: Read the instructions. Notice that the subject “you” is not necessary.
activities.content:
Use the base verb: “Open the page.” “Read the question.” “Write one sentence.”
For a negative instruction, use do not / don't: “Do not close the page.” “Don't forget your notes.”
Add please to sound polite: “Please check your answer.”
Use first, then, and finally to make the order clear.

activities.title: Use the learning platform step by step
activities.instructions: These are simple practice steps. Read them in order, then say them aloud.
activities.content:
First, open the revision pack.
Then, choose one day.
Read the grammar guide and the examples.
Choose an answer and read the feedback.
Practise a dialogue again with new words.
Finally, write a short response. Your written work is for review.

activities.title: Listen-style practice: simple directions
activities.instructions: Read the script aloud with a partner, or pause after each instruction and repeat it.

dialogue.speaker: Mia
dialogue.text: Please come in through the main entrance.

dialogue.speaker: Omar
dialogue.text: Okay. What do I do next?

dialogue.speaker: Mia
dialogue.text: Go up the stairs. Then turn left at the corner.

dialogue.speaker: Omar
dialogue.text: Is the room near the lift?

dialogue.speaker: Mia
dialogue.text: Yes. Do not use the lift today. The room is next to it.

questions.prompt: What should Omar do after he goes up the stairs?

activities.title: Dialogue: helping someone use a page
activities.instructions: Practise the helper role. Change the action in [brackets].

dialogue.speaker: Learner
dialogue.text: I cannot find the grammar practice.

dialogue.speaker: Helper
dialogue.text: First, choose Day 2.

dialogue.speaker: Learner
dialogue.text: I can see it. What next?

dialogue.speaker: Helper
dialogue.text: Read the examples. Then [choose an answer].

dialogue.speaker: Learner
dialogue.text: Thank you. I will practise the dialogue too.

days.title: Day 3 — Practise, write, and repeat
days.intro: Use place words and clear instructions together in a short everyday situation.

activities.title: Reading: a short shopping task
activities.instructions: Read the task. Notice the place prepositions and instructions.
activities.content: Noah is at a small shop. The basket is near the entrance. His shopping list is in his phone. First, take a basket. Then, find the bread on the shelf next to the milk. The receipt is on the counter after you pay. Do not leave your bag under the chair near the exit.

options: On a shelf next to the milk
Leave his bag under a chair

activities.title: Write clear instructions
activities.instructions: Write 4 short instructions for an invented place. Use at least two place words and two imperative verbs. This written work is for review.
activities.content: Starter ideas: “Put the book on…” “Go to…” “Turn…” “Do not…”

activities.title: Speak: give a simple direction
activities.instructions: Say four short instructions aloud. Choose an everyday place, such as a shop, room, station, or home. Use first, then, and finally.

activities.title: Dialogue: a useful everyday direction
activities.instructions: Say both roles. Then replace the location and object in [brackets].

dialogue.speaker: Rina
dialogue.text: Can you tell me where the [pharmacy] is?

dialogue.speaker: Kai
dialogue.text: Yes. Go straight ahead and turn right at the corner.

dialogue.speaker: Rina
dialogue.text: Is it near the [station]?

dialogue.speaker: Kai
dialogue.text: Yes. It is between the station and the café.

dialogue.speaker: Rina
dialogue.text: Great. Thank you.

patterns: Can you tell me where [the pharmacy] is?
